lane: V11P A2 -- publication identity and denominator reconciliation

defect.summary: The frozen V10 canonical_scored_payload keyed the trial key on arm_config_id (control_mode) alone; StrategyIdentity.config was entirely outside the key. M01-N (neighbour) shared control_mode='anchor' with M01-A while neighbour_mode lived only in config, so both arms collapsed onto one trial_key_sha256 and the computed neighbour was refused with duplicate_trial_key_already_published -- scored but never published.
defect.documented_effect: 3 cells computed, 2 published, 1 computed-unpublished; ledger denominator 119, scientifically observed 120 (PLAN section 0).
defect.regression_pin: tests/test_v11p_a2_publication.py::test_v1_keying_collides_arms_v2_keying_distinguishes_them proves three arm identities sharing arm_config_id collapse to ONE v1 key and produce THREE distinct v2 keys.

fields_added_to_key_payload: arm_id (explicit, mandatory under v2; argument or StrategyIdentity.arm_id)
arm_config_digest (sha256 over the versioned canonical arm payload)
arm_config_digest_inputs: schema (v11.arm_config_digest.v1 -- the digest definition itself is versioned)
config (the ENTIRE identity.config mapping, canonicalised verbatim)
identity_v2_spec.deliberately_excluded_from_digest: window_start_iso/window_end_iso -- cell fields, already inside the full trial key, so the digest stays comparable across cells.
fail_closed_rules: v2 without a resolvable non-empty arm_id raises ContractViolation
a whitespace-only arm_id argument raises ContractViolation
identity.arm_id padded with whitespace raises ContractViolation at construction
identity_version='v1' with an arm raises ContractViolation (v1 key space is frozen for historical rows)
unknown identity_version raises ContractViolation (no silent fallback)
identity_v2_spec.backward_compatibility: Omitting the arm reproduces the frozen v1 payload/key byte-for-byte (legacy_v1_payload pins the v1 key set and refuses shape drift). No historical ledger byte is rewritten; the historical row stays first and byte-identical in the append-only file (proved by test).
identity_v2_spec.concurrency: All check-then-append critical sections (publish_trial, record_trial_observation) run under one process-local RLock, so exactly-once holds for racing in-process publishers (proved by two concurrent-append tests). Cross-process writers to one ledger file remain outside this guarantee per factory concurrency policy (PLAN section 5.2: one writer per worktree).

reconciliation_decision.option_chosen: preferred option 1: explicit provenance-linked historical observation/amendment ACCEPTED BY the ledger schema
reconciliation_decision.mechanism: Append-only kind-less row (schema=v11.trial_observation.v1, verdict=TRIAL_OBSERVATION_AMENDMENT) built by m01_neighbour_amendment_entry from research/control/v10r_run/family_terminal_m01.json. research/protocol/registry.validate_entry_kind accepts kind-less rows; global_ledger.append_verified accepts them (non-null experiment_id + verdict). The row can therefore never be counted by published_cell_rows (kind CELL_RESULT) while denominator_split counts it toward the observed denominator.
reconciliation_decision.reason: The ledger schema demonstrably accepts provenance-linked observations, so the fallback (freezing observed_denominator=120 as a first-class consumer field) was unnecessary; the amendment keeps the evidence IN the ledger with byte-exact provenance (terminal artifact sha256) instead of only in a constant.
provenance_guarantees: M01-N metric values (net_return_sum=-515951.9347, expectancy_per_day=-1413.5669, max_drawdown=515951.9347) are copied verbatim from the documented terminal artifact and pin-checked against frozen constants; a drifted artifact is refused, never re-scored
status COMPUTED_UNPUBLISHED_CONTRACT_GAP, publish_stage and root_cause are carried verbatim; rescore_forbidden=true
dedupe key embeds the terminal artifact sha256, so re-running reconciliation is a no-op
supersede rule: an observation whose observed_trial_key_sha256 later appears as a published row no longer counts toward observed_unpublished, so a trial is counted exactly once overall

resulting_denominators.constants: M01_FROZEN_PUBLISHED_DENOMINATOR=119, M01_FROZEN_OBSERVED_DENOMINATOR=120 (research/v11/publication_identity.py); statistical consumers read denominator_view(ledger)

reconciliation_decision.historical_bytes_untouched: The real registry was never written by this lane; tests prove historical rows survive byte-for-byte as a prefix when v2 rows are appended after them.

changed_files: research/adapter_v10/protocol.py (minimal identity edit: optional declared arm_id field + whitespace guard; public_payload untouched so historical artifact views are stable)
research/adapter_v10/publish.py (versioned key resolution, observe_unpublished accounting, record_trial_observation, denominator_view, process-local exactly-once lock)
research/v11/publication_identity.py (new: v2 identity + digest, v1 readability pins, trial observations, M01 amendment, denominator split)

regression_sanity.note: targeted regression check over the two edited modules; full pytest suite intentionally NOT run by this lane (A1 runs it at integration)

test_summary.post_test_tree_state: no tracked file mutated by any test run (synthetic ledgers under tmp_path only)

deliverable_map.D5_migration_fault_tests: collision: test_v1_keying_collides_arms_v2_keying_distinguishes_them; missing arm id: test_v2_refuses_missing_blank_or_padded_arm_ids; digest drift: test_digest_drift_yields_distinct_keys_and_separate_publications; duplicate replay: test_publishing_all_three_arms_under_v2_is_exactly_once; concurrent append: test_concurrent_publish_of_one_trial_appends_exactly_once, test_concurrent_distinct_arms_append_without_corruption

assumptions: The interrupted first attempt left publish.py calling an undefined record_trial_observation; this lane completed it (plus the exactly-once lock and denominator_view) and kept the rest of the partial design after critical review.
publish_trial(arm_id='') is the API default meaning 'no explicit argument', so it falls back to a DECLARED identity.arm_id by design; the fail-closed missing-arm case is no declared arm anywhere.
Cross-process concurrent writers to one ledger file remain out of scope (factory concurrency policy assigns one writer per worktree); in-process thread concurrency is now exactly-once.

The real global registry was never written; the 119/120 reconciliation is proven on a synthetic ledger seeded to mirror the frozen M01 state, and the amendment entry itself is produced from the real terminal artifact's bytes.
